doc.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

title: Hearing the senior jazz ensemble and falling in love with jazz
summary: Watching Todd play valve trombone with the senior jazz ensemble made Watkins want to be a trombonist and a improviser; the repertoire was Basie-style high school jazz.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well it was good that they brought me in the high school, it’s nice to have something that you feel like you belong to. Even before classes started I had a sense of belonging to the band you know? And that first year of marching band was really exciting and then it turned out that all my friends were trombone players. So I wanted to be in the trombone section. And there was kind of a light bulb moment where as a sophomore they had a seniors perform for us. Like they brought in all the music kids and they had the high school jazz, the senior jazz ensemble perform for us, and that was that moment. And I’ll never forget, the guy’s name was Todd. He played lead trombone but he played valve trombone. And everything came together. Like I thought okay, I already know how to play tuba, I know I can play that valve trombone, this can get me out of the tuba section into the trombone section, and at the same time right at that moment I fell in love with the music. And so from that time up until today I’ve been listening to jazz every single day of my life.
Do you recall what arrangements, what was the style back then?

You know they did a lot of — the band director and the repertoire there was usually stuff like Count Basie, you know repertoire kind of standardized high school jazz repertoire, repertoire maybe a Thad Jones thing would sneak in, but mostly Basie kind of, that kind

of stuff. And that moment, the other component of that experience at that moment was he was improvising. He was taking a solo. And it just had meaning to me. And then ever since then everything I do, and I mean I’m an ensemble player as well, but my kind of my motivation, my fuel for practicing is so that I can exist in the landscape of improvisation you know. But yeah, so that moment, I’ll never forget it, I’ll never forget that picture there of standing there with all these other students and just having that, that’s what I’m going to do. You know? So I never questioned it after that.
